description: Search log and authority register for account-core contested questions C1, C2, C4, C10 and debt-collector status (milestone step A3). Every search is recorded, including those that found nothing.
citator: No paid citator (KeyCite/Shepard's) available. Later-history checks are open-web searches for citing cases; see each authority's later_history field.

searches.query: "1950.5" "bad faith" "shall not be entitled to claim any amount of the security" court of appeal
searches.result: No relevant result; only unrelated federal circuit insurance bad-faith opinions. No appellate decision construing (h)(7) located.

searches.query: "Granberry v. Islay Investments bad faith landlord setoff security deposit later case 1950.5 Court of Appeal"
searches.result: Returned Granberry itself (Stanford SCOCAL), secondary commentary, a Santa Barbara Superior Court tentative ruling (23CV03826) and the 1993 Court of Appeal Granberry opinion on FindLaw. No later appellate treatment of fn. 6.

searches.query: "Granberry v. Islay Investments" security deposit bad faith
searches.result: Justia copies of Granberry (1995) 9 Cal.4th 738 and Granberry I (1984) 161 Cal.App.3d 382; FindLaw copy of the 1993 Court of Appeal opinion (superseded by grant of review; not citable) which discusses the bad-faith jury instruction; commentary. No later appellate decision on bad-faith landlords' rights.

searches.query: California Court of Appeal 2025 security deposit "1950.5" "bad faith" AB 2801 photographs opinion (start_date 2025-01-01)
searches.result: One secondary digest page (verdict.com); WebFetch 403, Nimble extract timed out. No appellate decision after AB 2801 located.

searches.query: "1950.5" "bad faith" security, limited to 2025 onward (as_ylo=2025)
searches.result: Blocked: redirected to Google sign-in wall. No result.

searches.result: Scholar returned 'did not match any articles' (no California opinion citing subdivision (h)(7) in that form).

searches.query: "1950.5" "not be entitled to claim any amount of the security" (two attempts, vx10 and vx8 drivers)
searches.result: Both blocked by Google sign-in wall.

searches.query: "1950.5" "bad faith" "not be entitled to claim"
searches.result: Nimble timed out (60s). No result.

searches.query: "1950.5" "bad faith" "not be entitled to claim any amount of the security" opinion (Justia, courts.ca.gov, GovInfo, Casetext, AnyLaw, CaseMine, Leagle, FindLaw, vLex)
searches.result: Only statute copies (FindLaw, CaseMine). No opinion quoting (h)(7) located.

searches.query: California appellate court 2025 OR 2026 security deposit decision "1950.5" landlord bad faith published opinion AB 2801 photographs
searches.result: Bill text, SJUD analysis, landlord/tenant blogs. No 2025-2026 appellate decision on (h)(7).

searches.query: AB 2801 (2023-2024) bill analysis list; Assembly Floor Analysis (concurrence, as amended Aug 23, 2024) retrieved by form POST
searches.result: Floor analysis confirms Senate amendments were chaptering-only (SB 611 conflicts), so the SJUD analysis of the Apr 25, 2024 version describes the enacted (h)(7). Saved. SJUD analysis (June 11, 2024) also saved: says (h)(7) 'does not require strict adherence; just a good faith attempt to comply' and that a good-faith violator may offset (citing 250 L.L.C. v. PhotoPoint, 131 Cal.App.4th 702, 727).

searches.query: Chaptered AB 2801 (Stats. 2024 ch. 280) text already saved at j1/lanes/enactments/sources/202320240AB2801.txt
searches.result: Legislative Counsel's Digest describes (h)(7) more broadly than its text: 'prohibit the landlord from making a claim against the tenant or the security if the landlord, in bad faith, fails to comply'. Enacted text: 'shall not be entitled to claim any amount of the security'. Section 1 intent: landlords not to subsidize improvements with deposits.

searches.query: "250 L.L.C. v. PhotoPoint Corp." 131 Cal.App.4th 702
searches.result: Located on Justia (original A105231 and modification A105231M), CaseMine, vLex, FindLaw, Leagle. Commercial lease under Civ 1950.7.

searches.query: "Ingalls v. Bell" security deposit bad faith 1950.5
searches.result: No case of that name found; results were the statute and general web pages. Existence of an 'Ingalls v. Bell' deposit decision not confirmed by this search.

searches.query: "Kovarik v. DeVaul" security deposit
searches.result: No relevant result (dictionary and unrelated deposit pages). Existence not confirmed.

searches.query: "Orozco v. Casimiro" 121 Cal.App.4th Supp. 7 late fee security deposit bad faith
searches.result: Orozco located (App. Div., L.A. Super. Ct., June 24, 2004): an unlawful detainer about a late-fee clause. Leagle page is paywalled after the first paragraph; text sought elsewhere.

searches.query: "1950.5" "bad faith" "property manager" security deposit (as_sdt=4,5)
searches.result: 7 results: Runnymede Holdings v. Foster (2023) 96 Cal.App.5th Supp. 1 (published App. Div.); Thannhaeuser v. TKH Zuma (2d Dist. 2024, no reporter cite = unpublished); SM 10000 Property v. Pecci (2d Dist. 2026, no reporter cite); Alcoser v. Thomas (1st Dist. 2011, unpublished); Harris v. Capital Growth (1991) 52 Cal.3d 1142 (passing cite). Scholar case pages require Google sign-in, so texts must be fetched elsewhere.

searches.query: "bad faith" "1950.5" "security deposit" definition
searches.result: Granberry (1995); Bauman v. Islay (1973) 30 Cal.App.3d 752; Granberry I (1984); People ex rel. Smith v. Parkmerced (1988) 198 Cal.App.3d 683; Runnymede Holdings v. Foster (2023) 96 Cal.App.5th Supp. 1; Peviani v. Arbors at California Oaks (2021) 62 Cal.App.5th 874; unpublished: De Carlo v. Kosser (2013), Grabowiec v. Schopmeyer (2015), Marie-Chantal (2010). No published decision defining bad faith for 1950.5 seen in snippets.

searches.query: "Leaser v. Prime Ascot" property management restitution security deposit
searches.result: Only hit: GovInfo copy of Brooks ECF 56 citing Leaser. Followed GovInfo package USCOURTS-caed-2_20-cv-02502; ECF 60 (June 12, 2024) located and saved (official).

searches.query: USCOURTS-caed-2_20-cv-02502 (Leaser v. Prime Ascot) items 0-8
searches.result: Nine court-published orders 2022-2024; item 7 = ECF 60 (June 12, 2024), the order Brooks cites. Item 8 (July 19, 2024) is a stipulation. No later merits ruling in the GovInfo package as of retrieval.

searches.result: No case law; bill text, lease forms and guides only.

searches.result: First attempt: Google robot check; second: sign-in wall. No result.

searches.query: "1950.5" security deposit "bad faith" statutory damages "one-year" OR "one year" statute of limitations "340" penalty California
searches.result: Only Granberry and practitioner/blog pages; none states an appellate holding on the period for (m) damages.

searches.query: security deposit 1950.5 claim "Code of Civil Procedure section 340" OR "section 338" limitations tenant statutory damages court of appeal
searches.result: No deposit-specific authority. General limitation pages; County of San Diego v. Sanfax (1977) 19 Cal.3d 862 surfaced (penalty/forfeiture context).

searches.query: "Prudential Home Mortgage Co. v. Superior Court" 66 Cal.App.4th 1236 penalty one-year statute 340 section 2941
searches.result: Located (4th Dist., Div. 3, 1998). Saved from LawLink mirror. Holds the mandatory $300 forfeiture in Civ 2941(d) is a penalty under CCP 340(1); states the 'settled rule' that statutes giving damages additional to actual losses (double/treble) are penal; rejects MacManus v. A.E. Realty Partners.

searches.query: "Menefee v. Ostawari" 228 Cal.App.3d 239 one-year statute penalty
searches.result: Located (1st Dist., Div. 3, 1991), a landlord-tenant (SF rent ordinance treble damages) case. Saved from LawLink. Holds mandatory treble damages are a penalty (CCP 340(1)) but, following Holland v. Nelson, discretionary multiple damages are not.

searches.query: "Holland v. Nelson" 5 Cal.App.3d 308 treble damages discretionary statute of limitations 340
searches.result: Located (1st Dist., Div. 4, 1970). Saved from Justia. Discretionary treble damages under the Dance Act are not a penalty; CCP 338 (3 years) applies, partly because plaintiff could not otherwise know the period until the court exercised its discretion.
